fixes.explanation: "Spoken" is the word, friend. The LORD says, "For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has." (Job 42:7) Job's words get the LORD's approval there, and the three friends' words don't.

"Written" isn't the word, friend. The LORD says, "For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has." (Job 42:7) The LORD is talking about what they said, so the word is "spoken," not "written."

I would pay good money to hear Eliphaz sing, but that's not what the text says. The LORD says, "For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has." (Job 42:7) The word is "spoken," not "sung."

That's it, baker! The LORD says, "Then My servant Job will pray for you…" (Job 42:8) The friends are the ones who need the prayer, and Job is the one who gives it. The LORD says He will accept Job's prayer.

Foot washing is a good guess, friend, but it's not in this verse. The LORD says, "Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer…" (Job 42:8) Job's part is prayer, and the LORD says He will accept it.

No refusing here, friend. The friends did as the LORD told them, "and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer." (Job 42:9) Refusing would be a plot twist, and this verse doesn't give us one. The word is "accepts."

Yes, baker! "After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions." (Job 42:10) Notice what comes first: Job prayed for his friends. Then the verse says the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.

Removing is the opposite of what happens here, friend. "After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions." (Job 42:10) This verse goes toward more, not less. The word is "restores."

A lamb and a jar of oil would make a nice gift basket, friend, but they're not what the verse lists. The text says, "And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring." (Job 42:11) That's the gift from each one. They also consoled and comforted him over all the adversity.

A nice outfit, friend, but a robe and sandals aren't what the verse lists. "And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring." (Job 42:11) Every guest came with a piece of silver and a gold ring. They also consoled and comforted him in the same verse.

True, baker! "So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first." (Job 42:12) Then the verse lists what Job owned: 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys. The latter days were blessed even more than the first.

Right, baker! "…their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers." (Job 42:15) Job had seven sons and three daughters. The daughters received an inheritance among their brothers. That verse comes right after their names, Jemimah, Keziah and Keren-happuch.

The text goes further than that, friend. "After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation." (Job 42:16) Job saw his children and their children, and the verse keeps going to the fourth generation. The answer is the fourth generation.

Tenth would be a LOT of generations, friend, but the text says less. "After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation." (Job 42:16) Job saw to the fourth generation.
